title: Light Time and Horizons
subtitle: Lorentz signal geometry under explicit event and clock identifications
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: A complex binary record has a Lorentz cone and a hyperbolic projective interior. We specify the operational bridges that identify this structure with physical event displacements, null signals and calibrated clocks. The determinant then supplies a conformal Lorentz metric, while a tangent-only Lorentz-invariant clock selects proper time up to scale. Doppler frequencies and normalized binary readouts have a common cone pairing, with different physical calibrations. We prove the distinction among harmonic sky probability, local photon-number density and bolometric radiation moments, give an exact acceleration-horizon criterion, and isolate the Fourier amplitude ratio produced by exponential redshift from the additional quantum assumptions needed for thermality. Positive maps and finite-rank baths yield exact boundary and cumulative-resource inequalities. Within flat scalar wave models, positivity together with sharp retarded support selects three spatial dimensions. The conclusions are closed within their stated operational and physical models; no identification of all qubit operations with frame changes, all radiation with a finite moment state, or all horizons with thermal states is assumed.
conditions: Invertible tangent-to-Hermitian event solder identifies physical future and null displacement cones.
Global special-relativistic results use a flat affine event structure and constant solder.
Null phase covector and calibrated detector velocity contraction define received frequency.
Tangent-only Lorentz-invariant clock uses a common calibration, excluding history, acceleration and metric-derivative corrections.
Harmonic angular probability and bolometric energy intensity are separate measures; P4 requires the radiation transformation model.
Acceleration horizon criterion uses a future-complete collinear proper-time worldline in flat spacetime.
Mellin amplitude ratio is a regulated nonzero-frequency statement; quantum thermality requires field-state, normalization and detector/KMS premises.
Finite-bath resource bound uses fixed finite system dimension, full-rank baths, unitary coupling and partial trace.
Three-dimensional propagation selection is conditional on the flat scalar massless wave operator and positive retarded response.
Moment nonclosure theorem applies to the specified collisionless ray model, not every finite observer.
D3 photon-number density requires a finite positive isotropic-rest scalar kinetic occupation and equal-time local sampling; generic detector crossing counts can carry other weights.
